rounds.proof_sketch: With fixed shape [16, 256, 256], dim2=256. Kernel launched with block_size=256, so blockDim.x=256 and blockDim.z=1. Original: elements_per_thread = (256+256-1)/256 = 511/256 = 1. Mutated: elements_per_thread = (256+1-1)/256 = 256/256 = 1. Both formulas produce identical value of 1.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes `blockDim.x` to `blockDim.z` in the numerator of the ceiling division formula for computing elements_per_thread. However, with the fixed input shape [16, 256, 256] and block_size=256, we have dim2=256, blockDim.x=256, and blockDim.z=1. The original formula (dim2 + blockDim.x - 1) / blockDim.x = (256 + 255) / 256 = 1, and the mutated formula (dim2 + blockDim.z - 1) / blockDim.x = (256 + 0) / 256 = 1. Both compute elements_per_thread = 1, meaning each of the 256 threads processes exactly one element, covering all dim2=256 elements correctly. The mutation only affects control-flow parameters that happen to evaluate identically under this specific fixed configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed shape [16, 256, 256]. The mutation would only cause behavioral differences if dim2 were not evenly divisible by blockDim.x (256), but dim2=256 is exactly divisible by 256, so ceiling division and floor division produce the same result.
rounds.recommendations: When testing CUDA kernels with parameterized dimensions, include test configurations where dimension sizes are NOT evenly divisible by block sizes to expose ceiling-division related mutations. For this kernel, testing with dim2 values like 257 or 300 would expose the mutation.
